newsitem.title: USA: Pinnacle West to call for stock buyback.
newsitem.headline: Pinnacle West to call for stock buyback.

text.p: Pinnacle West Capital Corp said on Wednesday that its management would recommend that the board of directors declare a stock buyback program to start next year.

The company said in a statement that management expected to make the recommendation in the first quarter of 1997. Details, including the timing and the amount for repurchase, would be made available when approved.
The company also announced a 10 percent increase in the yearly dividend, to $1.10.

The statement said the company planned to continue increasing its dividend "at a pace that is well above the electric utility industry average and to increase earnings per share through operating results and stock repurchases.
"For at least the next several years, the plans include annual dividend increases by relatively consistent dollar amounts."

The company said it will report third quarter earnings on approximately Oct 23, and in the quarter will record a $14.3 million, or $0.16 per share, extraordinary charge as a result of August's refinancing of its remaining $150 million of high-coupon debt.
For the full year, the company will record prepayment penalties of $20.3 million after tax, or $0.23 per share).

Chairman Richard Snell said the company is confident of its prospects for earnings progress in 1996 and 1997 despite the prepayment penalties and a settlement agreement with the Arizona Corporation Commission earlier this year, which took effect on July 1 and included a 3.4 percent rate reduction and accelerated amortization of regulatory assets.
